The finite checks support, but do not replace, this universal proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest established statement in Marberg (2010) counts supernormal/unitriangular ideals for prime q. This new claim is the prime-subfield-additive size distribution at arbitrary extension degree, and shows the numerically sharp difference at q=4. The 2018 brace-ideals paper supplies motivation and definition, not an inspected full formula. Targeted published-record and literature comparisons found no implication establishing the nonprime distribution; possible unindexed equivalents remain an explicit risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent enumerative statement in associative-ideal or supernormal-subgroup literature may exist.

The primary full-text comparison was focused on sections bearing the same objects and claims; comprehensive global literature uniqueness is not established.

value.rationale: The exact complete additive ideal-size polynomial is an intrinsic structural invariant, necessary for interpreting radical-brace ideals over nonprime fields and not recoverable from the q-linear ideal counts. The q=4 ring already has 3011 additive ideals versus 59 scalar-linear ideals; the all-p,m formula classifies their sizes and exhibits the role of hidden prime-subfield subspaces. This is an all-degree structural enumeration, not an arbitrary slice.
